	<h1><a href="http://comonad.com/reader" title="The Comonad.Reader">The Comonad.Reader</a></h1>

	<div id="content">

						<div class="post">
				<p class="post-date">Wed 26 Mar 2008</p>
<div class="post-info"><h2 class="post-title"><a href="http://comonad.com/reader/2008/higher-order-abstract-syntax-a-la-carte/" rel="bookmark" title="Permanent Link: Higher-Order Abstract Syntax à la Carte">Higher-Order Abstract Syntax à la Carte</a></h2>
Posted by Edward Kmett under <a href="http://comonad.com/reader/category/category-theory/" title="View all posts in Category Theory" rel="category tag">Category Theory</a> ,  <a href="http://comonad.com/reader/category/haskell/" title="View all posts in Haskell" rel="category tag">Haskell</a> <br/><a href="http://comonad.com/reader/2008/higher-order-abstract-syntax-a-la-carte/#comments" title="Comment on Higher-Order Abstract Syntax à la Carte">[393] Comments</a>&nbsp;</div>
<div class="post-content">
	<p>You may recall the definition for an exponential functor from my previous entry, which can also be viewed, I suppose, as functors in the<br />
category of right-invertible functions in Haskell.</p>
<pre class="haskell">&nbsp;
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">class</span> ExpFunctor f <span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">where</span>
	xmap :: <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>a -&gt; b<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> -&gt; <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>b -&gt; a<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> -&gt; f a -&gt; f b
&nbsp;</pre>
<p>Clarifying the above, an instance of ExpFunctor should satisfy the slightly generalized version of the Functor laws from Control.Monad:</p>
<pre class="haskell">&nbsp;
xmap <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:id"><span style="font-weight: bold;">id</span></a> <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:id"><span style="font-weight: bold;">id</span></a> = <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:id"><span style="font-weight: bold;">id</span></a>
xmap f g . xmap f' g' = xmap <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>f . f'<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>g' . g<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span>
&nbsp;</pre>
<p>Since we like to apply xmap to a pair of functions such that f . g = id, as in the Fegaras/Sheard case, we get:</p>
<pre class="haskell">&nbsp;
xmap f g . xmap g f
	= xmap <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>f . g<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>f . g<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> <span style="color: #5d478b; font-style: italic;">-- by second xmap law</span>
        = xmap <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:id"><span style="font-weight: bold;">id</span></a> <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:id"><span style="font-weight: bold;">id</span></a> 	       <span style="color: #5d478b; font-style: italic;">-- by f . g = id</span>
	= <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:id"><span style="font-weight: bold;">id</span></a>		       <span style="color: #5d478b; font-style: italic;">-- by first xmap law</span>
&nbsp;</pre>
<p>In any event, what I thought what I'd do today is note that Wouter Swierstra's <a href="http://www.cs.nott.ac.uk/~wss/Publications/DataTypesALaCarte.pdf">Data Types a la Carte</a> approach works over exponential functors.</p>
<p><span id="more-45"></span></p>
<p>Swierstra's main definition looks something like:</p>
<pre class="haskell">&nbsp;
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">data</span> <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>f :+: g<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> e = Inl <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>f e<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> | Inr <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>g e<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span>
&nbsp;
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">instance</span> <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span><a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#t:Functor"><span style="background-color: #efefbf; font-weight: bold;">Functor</span></a> f, <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#t:Functor"><span style="background-color: #efefbf; font-weight: bold;">Functor</span></a> g<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> =&gt; <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#t:Functor"><span style="background-color: #efefbf; font-weight: bold;">Functor</span></a> <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>f :+: g<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> <span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">where</span>
	<a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:fmap"><span style="font-weight: bold;">fmap</span></a> f <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>Inl e<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> = Inl <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span><a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:fmap"><span style="font-weight: bold;">fmap</span></a> f e<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span>
	<a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:fmap"><span style="font-weight: bold;">fmap</span></a> f <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>Inr e<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> = Inr <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span><a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:fmap"><span style="font-weight: bold;">fmap</span></a> f e<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span>
&nbsp;</pre>
<p>This permits the obvious analogue:</p>
<pre class="haskell">&nbsp;
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">instance</span> <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>ExpFunctor f, ExpFunctor g<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> =&gt; ExpFunctor <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>f :+: g<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> <span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">where</span>
	xmap f g <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>Inl e<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> = Inl <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>xmap f g e<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span>
	xmap f g <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>Inr e<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> = Inr <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>xmap f g e<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span>
&nbsp;</pre>
<p>With this we can quickly encode the untyped lambda calculus:</p>
<pre class="haskell">&nbsp;
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">newtype</span> Lam a = Lam <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>a -&gt; a<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span>
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">instance</span> ExpFunctor Lam <span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">where</span>
	xmap f g <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>Lam k<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> = Lam <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>f . k . g<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span>
&nbsp;
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">data</span> App a = App a a
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">instance</span> <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#t:Functor"><span style="background-color: #efefbf; font-weight: bold;">Functor</span></a> App <span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">where</span>
	<a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:fmap"><span style="font-weight: bold;">fmap</span></a> f <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>App a b<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> = App <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>f a<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>f b<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span>
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">instance</span> ExpFunctor App <span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">where</span>
	xmap = <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:const"><span style="font-weight: bold;">const</span></a> . <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:fmap"><span style="font-weight: bold;">fmap</span></a>
&nbsp;</pre>
<p>(Even better we could define a generic Bind and Binary functors, and newtype to get Lam and App)</p>
<p>and we can encode the recursion using any of the ways we previously established to tie the knot (Nu f, ForAll (Rec f), ForAll (Elim f)).</p>
<p>The rest of the a la carte stuff remains unchanged.</p>
<p>We then get a definition of catamorphism 'for free', due to the definitions from the other day. </p>
<p>From there we can define a fairly generic pretty printing framework.</p>
<pre class="haskell">&nbsp;
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">class</span> ShowAlgebra f <span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">where</span>
    showAlgebra :: f <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span><span style="color: green;">&#91;</span><a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#t:String"><span style="background-color: #efefbf; font-weight: bold;">String</span></a><span style="color: green;">&#93;</span> -&gt; <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#t:String"><span style="background-color: #efefbf; font-weight: bold;">String</span></a><span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> -&gt; <span style="color: green;">&#91;</span><a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#t:String"><span style="background-color: #efefbf; font-weight: bold;">String</span></a><span style="color: green;">&#93;</span> -&gt; <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#t:String"><span style="background-color: #efefbf; font-weight: bold;">String</span></a>
&nbsp;
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">instance</span> <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>ShowAlgebra f, ShowAlgebra g<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> =&gt; ShowAlgebra <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>f :+: g<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> <span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">where</span>
    showAlgebra <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>Inl e<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> = showAlgebra e
    showAlgebra <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>Inr e<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> = showAlgebra e
&nbsp;
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">instance</span> <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>Cata f <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>ForAll t<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span>, ShowAlgebra f<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> =&gt; <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#t:Show"><span style="background-color: #efefbf; font-weight: bold;">Show</span></a> <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>ForAll t<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> <span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">where</span>
    <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:show"><span style="font-weight: bold;">show</span></a> x = cata showAlgebra <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>runForAll x<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> vars
&nbsp;</pre>
<p>And then we can derive particular instances for the untyped lambda calculus we slapped together above:</p>
<pre class="haskell">&nbsp;
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">instance</span> ShowAlgebra Lam <span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">where</span>
    showAlgebra <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>Lam k<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>v:vars<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> =
        <span style="color: #3c7331;">&quot;(<span style="">\\</span><span style="">\\</span>&quot;</span> ++ v ++ <span style="color: #3c7331;">&quot;. &quot;</span> ++ k <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span><a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:const"><span style="font-weight: bold;">const</span></a> v<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> vars ++ <span style="color: #3c7331;">&quot;)&quot;</span>
&nbsp;
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">instance</span> ShowAlgebra App <span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">where</span>
    showAlgebra <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>App a b<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> vars =
        <span style="color: #3c7331;">&quot;(&quot;</span> ++ a vars ++ <span style="color: #3c7331;">&quot; &quot;</span> ++ b vars ++ <span style="color: #3c7331;">&quot;)&quot;</span>
&nbsp;</pre>
<p>Then using the combinators from the other day:</p>
<pre class="haskell">&nbsp;
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">type</span> Term a = Elim <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>Lam :+: App<span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> a
<span style="color: #06c; font-weight: bold;">type</span> Expr = ForAll Term
&nbsp;
app_id_id :: Term a
app_id_id = app <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>lam <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:id"><span style="font-weight: bold;">id</span></a><span style="color: green;">&#41;</span> <span style="color: green;">&#40;</span>lam <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:id"><span style="font-weight: bold;">id</span></a><span style="color: green;">&#41;</span>
<span style="color: #5d478b; font-style: italic;">-- for suitable definitions of app and lam a la the a la Carte paper.</span>
&nbsp;
main = <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:putStrLn"><span style="font-weight: bold;">putStrLn</span></a> . <a href="http://haskell.org/ghc/docs/latest/html/libraries/base/Prelude.html#v:show"><span style="font-weight: bold;">show</span></a> $ safe app_id_id
&nbsp;</pre>
<p>Other algebra structures can be derived similarly.</p>
	<div class="post-info">
